level: stop-fence slice 5 drain wiring, declared remote client revocation in the hash chain before capture; component evidence only
componentAcceptance: The migration commit operation now persists bounded remoteClients and remoteClientsDigest. After exclusive-acquired it writes remote-revoke-requested, invokes the E98 adapter and verifies its complete result, then writes remote-revoke-completed before capture-started. An unconfirmed revoke produces blocked-drain with no capture and recovery does not duplicate the request. A real subprocess exit(86) after remote-revoke-requested resumes to exactly one completion before capture. A separate default-adapter test runs the full orchestration against a real Agent and reads back host revoked=1, so the production call path is covered without a test callback. The orchestration combination is 31 tests / 30 pass / 0 fail / 1 skipped; the full root regression has zero failures.
productAcceptance: None. This orders declared client revocation before capture; it does not prove draining of in-flight effects, other clients or machines, direct OS writers or all-domain stop-write. Activation and post-activation rollback stay unsupported. Scores remain 0/20, 1/63 and M0 11/12.
implementation: The immutable operation record binds the ordered remote client declarations and their SHA-256. Re-entry with a different declaration set is an operation mismatch.
The drain phase appends remote-revoke-requested before invoking the adapter and accepts only a complete, matching revoked result with declared credential admission and persistent exclusion true.
MIGRATION_REMOTE_CLIENT_* failures append blocked-drain and preserve the fence. Capture explicitly returns to drain whenever declared clients lack a completed record.

Recovery retains one request record, reuses the adapter's durable revoked state and appends one completion. The new crash-12 case uses a real child process exit(86), not an exception pretending to be a crash.

The default production adapter path is exercised by the complete orchestration with a real Agent, real CLI and real SQLite readback. Operations without remote clients retain the original 12-step chain.
testRuns: Existing orchestration plus two new drain tests, crash 12 and the real default-adapter test: 31 tests / 30 pass / 0 fail / 1 skipped.
Final npm test: phase one 1589/1585/0/4 and phase two 356/276/0/80; total 1943 tests, 1861 pass, 0 fail, 84 skipped.
limitations: Only explicitly declared clients are ordered by this drain. Unknown clients, other machines and direct OS writers are outside the evidence.
The chain proves request and readback ordering, not that effects already executing at revocation were drained or rolled back.
Remote deployment, other launcher/account closure, reboot, activation and post-activation rollback remain open.
No real user profile, model inference, production process, push or release was used.
